# Feed-forward and Generalizable Prediction

Also called: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting, Generalizable Gaussian Splatting, One-shot 3DGS

## Overview
Feed-forward and Generalizable Prediction refers to methods that predict 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) parameters directly from input images in a single forward pass, eliminating the iterative per-scene optimization required by standard 3DGS. This family solves the latency bottleneck of inverse volume rendering, enabling real-time novel-view synthesis and 3D reconstruction from sparse or uncalibrated inputs. Unlike iterative optimization methods, these models rely on learned priors from foundation models (e.g., MASt3R, DINOv2) or large-scale training on synthetic/real datasets to generalize across scenes. Key differentiators among siblings include handling uncalibrated inputs (e.g., [Splatt3R](16423-splatt3r.md), [ZeroGS](16425-zerogs.md)), resource efficiency (e.g., [RLSplat](16575-rlsplat.md)), or specific domain adaptations like human avatars (e.g., [HFGaussian](16422-hfgaussian.md)).

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the following mechanism:
1.  **Input Encoding:** Input images are processed by a shared encoder (typically a Vision Transformer or CNN) to extract multi-scale features. These features capture semantic and geometric cues necessary for 3D reasoning.
2.  **Direct Parameter Regression:** A decoder network predicts the Gaussian attributes ($\mu, s, r, \alpha, c$) directly from the encoded features. The output is a set of 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G}$ without iterative refinement.
3.  **Differentiable Rendering:** The predicted Gaussians are rendered into target views using differentiable rasterization (e.g., [Gaussian Splatting](8442-gaussian-geometry-parameters-prediction.md) rasterizer) to compute photometric losses during training.
4.  **Generalization:** Models are trained on large datasets to learn scene priors, allowing inference on unseen scenes without per-scene optimization.

## Subtopics

### [AnySplat Pipeline](12847-anysplat-pipeline.md)
AnySplat predicts a full set of 3D Gaussians, camera poses, and depth maps from uncalibrated input images in a single pass. It differs from siblings like [Splatt3R](16423-splatt3r.md) by explicitly predicting camera poses and depth alongside Gaussian parameters, using a differentiable voxelization module to stabilize rendering. It is chosen when pose-free novel-view synthesis is required without external SfM tools.

### [FineSplat](15257-finesplat.md)
FineSplat uses a two-stage dual-grouping strategy to balance local detail and global reasoning. It divides input views into fine-grained $4 \times 4$ patches and employs view-wise token grouping, followed by 3D spatial grouping. It sets itself apart by avoiding the cost of global attention while maintaining fine-grained information through serialized attention in 3D space. Choose it for high-fidelity reconstruction from multiple context views where global consistency and local detail are both critical.

### [SparSplat](15813-sparsplat.md)
SparSplat maps sparse input images (typically 3 views) directly to 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) parameters. It leverages foundation models like DINOv2 and MASt3R. It differs from [MVSGaussian](12847-anysplat-pipeline.md) by using 2DGS primitives, ensuring multi-view depth consistency for coherent TSDF mesh fusion. It is chosen when surface reconstruction (mesh extraction) is required alongside novel-view synthesis from sparse inputs.

### [HFGaussian](16422-hfgaussian.md)
HFGaussian is a human-centric framework that estimates 3D human avatars with integrated biomechanical features (skeleton, keypoints, dense pose) from sparse images. It distinguishes itself by decoupling photometric properties from biomechanical features via "feature splatting," allowing independent modeling of human features. It is chosen for real-time human avatar rendering without per-subject fine-tuning.

### [Splatt3R](16423-splatt3r.md)
Splatt3R predicts 3D Gaussian Splat parameters directly from a pair of uncalibrated natural images, extending the MASt3R foundation model with a parallel "Gaussian head." It solves pose-free novel view synthesis by predicting geometry offsets, covariances, opacities, and colors. It differs from siblings by employing a loss masking strategy to enable stable training and inference for extrapolated viewpoints beyond the stereo baseline.

### [ZeroGS](16425-zerogs.md)
ZeroGS trains 3DGS from hundreds of unposed and unordered images without SfM tools. It uses a pretrained foundation model (Spann3R) to predict dense 3D Gaussians and pointmaps, followed by incremental registration. It differs from siblings by regressing points in a global coordinate frame without aligning dense pairwise pointmaps, allowing it to handle hundreds of images on consumer hardware.

### [Shape Completion Training](16514-shape-completion-training.md)
This method predicts all 14 Gaussian attributes from partial input views using a decoder-based approach with a folding grid expansion. It distinguishes itself by predicting full Gaussian parameters directly from a frozen encoder's features via a transformer decoder, rather than relying on dense depth estimation or iterative optimization. It is chosen for scenarios with missing regions or masks in input views.

### [GlobalSplat](16571-globalsplat.md)
GlobalSplat aligns multi-view inputs into a fixed set of global latent scene tokens before decoding explicit 3D geometry. It aggregates inputs into 2048 latent tokens, then decodes them into 16K Gaussians. It sets itself apart by preventing representation bloat and ensuring global consistency through an "align first, decode later" approach, achieving a stronger quality-efficiency trade-off than methods relying on full self-attention.

### [RLSplat](16575-rlsplat.md)
RLSplat is a resource-linear, budget-controllable framework that generates exactly $B$ Gaussians for a given target budget. It uses a learned allocation policy to distribute Gaussians across local scene regions and a resource-linear decoder. It differs from prior budget-controllable methods by ensuring inference latency and memory scale linearly with $B$, making it suitable for AR/VR and robotics with strict resource constraints.

### 3D-aware Image Synthesis via Sparse Voxel Grids
A 3D-aware image synthesis generator that predicts color and density values on a sparse voxel grid, conditioned on camera pose [S1]. It uses a mapping network with 2 layers and 64 channels, reducing the channel base from StyleGAN2's 32768 to 4000 to account for higher parameter counts in 3D convolutions [S1]. Skip connections add an upsampled version of the output grid of the previous layer to the input of the next layer [S1]. The generator is conditioned on a camera pose represented by a rotation matrix and a translation vector, yielding a 12-dimensional input vector [S1]. It outputs coefficients of spherical harmonics for color, using degree 0 (single coefficient per color channel) [S1]. The density output is multiplied by a factor of 30 to facilitate generating high density values for sharp surfaces [S1]. Parameters: Channel base 4000, density multiplier 30, mapping network layers 2, mapping network channels 64, spherical harmonics degree 0 [S1].

### Deformation Field MLP
An MLP network $F_\theta$ that maps 3D Gaussian coordinates and time to deviations in position, rotation, and scaling [S2]. The input $x$ and time $t$ are processed through eight fully connected layers with ReLU activations and 256-dimensional hidden layers to output a 256-dimensional feature vector [S2]. The feature vector is concatenated with the input in the fourth layer [S2]. It is passed through three additional fully connected layers (without activation) to separately output offsets $\delta x, \delta r, \delta s$ for position, rotation, and scaling [S2]. Parameters: Hidden layer dimension 256, number of initial fully connected layers 8, number of output layers 3, activation function ReLU for hidden layers and none for output layers, additional storage compared to 3D Gaussians 2MB [S2]. It does not use grid/plane-based structures because dynamic scenes have higher rank than static scenes, and explicit point-based rendering exacerbates this rank [S2].

### RnD-Avatar
A 3DGS-based human avatar modeling framework that reconstructs animatable and relightable human avatars from monocular video by decomposing geometry and appearance attributes and using dynamic skinning weights for pose-variant deformation [S3]. It encodes Gaussian attributes using the Gaussian Attributes Encoder $D_G$, consisting of two sub-encoders $D_g$ and $D_a$ (MLPs) that take Gaussian position $x$ as input and output geometric and appearance attributes, respectively [S3]. It articulates the human avatar by applying Linear Blend Skinning (LBS) transformations using dynamic skinning weights $W_{\Theta_t}$ to deform 3D Gaussians from canonical space to posed space [S3]. It optimizes the avatar through a Physically-Based Rendering (PBR) process to optimize geometric attributes (position and normal) and appearance attributes (albedo, roughness, and visibility) [S3]. It renders photorealistic images given an environmental light by performing a PBR process on the optimized avatar [S3].

## Background
Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting emerged as a solution to the high computational cost of per-scene optimization in standard 3DGS. Early works like [Splatt3R](16423-splatt3r.md) and [ZeroGS](16425-zerogs.md) leveraged foundation models (MASt3R, DUSt3R/SpaNN3R) to provide geometric priors, enabling pose-free reconstruction. Subsequent methods focused on efficiency ([RLSplat](16575-rlsplat.md)), detail preservation ([FineSplat](15257-finesplat.md)), and domain-specific applications like human avatars ([HFGaussian](16422-hfgaussian.md), [RnD-Avatar](#rnd-avatar)) and dynamic scenes ([Deformation Field MLP](#deformation-field-mlp)). The field has evolved from simple regression of Gaussian parameters to complex architectures involving latent tokens, allocation policies, and hybrid representations (e.g., 2DGS in [SparSplat](15813-sparsplat.md)).
